newsitem.title: GERMANY: "God-inspired" neo-Nazi goes on trial in Germany.
newsitem.headline: "God-inspired" neo-Nazi goes on trial in Germany.

text.p: A 28-year-old German neo-Nazi, who claimed the Nordic god of war ordered him to commit crimes, went on trial on Friday charged with rape and murder.
Thomas Lemke, who belonged to several extreme right-wing groups, is accused of the murder of one man and two women, the rape of one of the women and attempted rape of the other.
Lemke, from the western town of Gladbeck, has confessed to the murders and said he also committed three others, although police have found no evidence of these supposed crimes.

"I must have been mad. I'm sorry. I cannot find any excuse. If I could give my life so that she (the first victim) was alive again then I would do so immediately," Lemke told the court, when asked how he felt about the crimes.
After Lemke's arrest last March, state prosecutors said he claimed he had been directed by Odin, the god of war and death in Norse mythology.

Lemke's first victim was a 25-year-old Dortmund woman whom he killed in August 1995. During the first day of the trial Lemke said he had forced his girlfriend, Bianca Weidemann, to help him strangle the woman in a wood.
He then struck the woman with a spade as she lay dying.
Weidemann is charged with murder and a former neo-Nazi friend, Marcel Muething, 26, is charged with aiding and abetting him.
But Lemke said Weidemann was more a victim than an accomplice and should not have been charged with murder.
Lemke said he planned the first killing to bind his girlfriend more closely to him.
"It had to be a murder because then she (Weidemann) would definitely not betray me. I was unimaginative at the time. The risks of a bank robbery were too big," Lemke said.
"I simply wanted to kill somebody. Somebody who was stupid enough to come along with me."
He said he had sliced off the woman's clothes with a knife and burned her belongings to prevent her from being identified.
Weidemann, 26, sobbed in court as she listened to the description of the murder and later confirmed it.
Lemke is also accused of stabbing a 22-year-old woman 91 times in her apartment in Bergisch Gladbach near Cologne last February. She had been wearing a badge bearing the slogan "Nazis out".
Lemke was arrested last March, two days after killing a former member of the neo-Nazi scene who had turned his back on the extremists and become a police informer.
